chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I scratched my head while I was in Ihram, so a louse fell down.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'What do you make upon me as expiation for it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And what do I make upon you for a louse? There is nothing upon you for it.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَجْعَلُ عَلَيَّ: You make upon me (as an expiation/penalty)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a louse while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that killing a louse while in Ihram incurs no expiation, highlighting the principle of proportional liability based on the creature's size and significance. This ruling distinguishes minor pests like lice from larger insects or animals, reflecting the Shia juristic approach to minimizing hardship for pilgrims. The dialogue underscores the practical flexibility within the sacred state of Ihram regarding everyday occurrences.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Al Qalanasy, from Ahmad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I rub my head and I am in Ihraam, so lice falls down’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘Which thing is upon me (as an expiation) with regards to it?’ Heasws said: ‘And Iasws did not make (anything to be) upon you with regards to lice. There is nothing upon you with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ahmad al-Qalanisiy from Ahmad ibn al-Walid from Aban from abu al-Jarud who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of scratching my head in the state of Ihram when a louse fell off. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’ I then asked, ‘What you want me to pay for it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I place nothing on you to pay for a louse. There is not anything for it upon you.’”
